newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE extends mission in Bosnia through 1997.
newsitem.headline: OSCE extends mission in Bosnia through 1997.

text.p: The European security organisation which supervised the first postwar elections in Bosnia said on Thursday it would extend its mission through next year to consolidate peace in the former Yugoslav republic.

Diplomats said envoys from the 54-nation Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), meeting in Vienna, agreed to extend the mission to Bosnia until December 31, 1997, and then to consider a further extension into 1998.
The OSCE, which also has responsibility for arms control in former Yugoslavia, is working alongside the NATO-led peace force and is expected to help run municipal elections due sometime next year.
Those polls, supposed to be held at the same time as national elections in September, were postponed by the OSCE because of what it said were widespread abuse of electoral rules in municipalities.
Major powers involved in Bosnia, meeting in Paris last week, had asked the OSCE to extend its mission.
